review_sample.scope: Independent-session teacher spot review, not independent ground truth or correctness proof. Selected inputs were rendered without targets. rule_reproduction.method: runpy.run_path(audit.py) with non-main run name, call expected(mechanism, facts), require exactly one matching option text and compare its ID with target. Producer main not run.
rule_reproduction.limitations: Same teacher generated generator and audit; facts not independently extracted from natural language. Only selected row text was solved before target comparison; all-target reproduction is consistency, not proof.

findings.title: Legitimate parameter variation, but substantial template redundancy
findings.detail: 163 trigram-Jaccard >= .65 pairs reproduced exactly; all within rule groups, none cross-split. All 163 pairs have distinct structured facts and the same mechanism; no identical-fact target conflicts. Read strongest/weakest flagged pairs per each of 9 groups (18 displays, 17 unique pairs). Priority changes, zero/boundary tariffs, modular wraps, score thresholds, empty symmetric differences, endpoint overlaps, weighted remainders, ignored events and voting ties are meaningful cases. Same outcome on different facts is not a conflict. 135 pairs come from routing, set reconciliation and state-machine groups alone. No clear quota-only filler found in sampled pairs, but redundancy lowers effective diversity; motive and semantic nonredundancy of every pair are not established.

findings.title: Cross-family domain overlap is real; copied source scenarios not established
findings.detail: No exact normalized full-input duplicate, no repeated state/question warning, no cross-family trigram pair >= .65; maximum cross-family state similarity .035714. Manual scenario comparison found intent train dog boarding g09 versus sentiment validation boarding g26, and intent train astronomy g17 versus sentiment validation observatory g27. Events differ (extend booking or borrow telescope versus lost blanket or queue criticism); no shared named source/entity/event is established. Seed desk, bike workshop and pottery also recur across families. Current group isolation is source-group isolation, not topic-disjoint isolation. Do not claim cross-family domain-disjoint validation or semantic deduplication completeness.

findings.title: Sentiment revision fixes published template/candidate shortcuts; explicit cues remain
findings.detail: All 120 revisions preserve original state, split, group, subject and teacher target class; source-to-revision map covers 120 unique published IDs. Each revised row has exactly all four semantic classes and the neutral subject-specific question. Parent hashes match. Original sentiment shards are excluded from manifest and reviewed only as parent lineage, not as published data. Revised states still often say delighted, disappointed, mixed, or explicitly state both views; neutral examples are strongly factual. Clean synthetic English and limited candidate paraphrases remain easy lexical shortcuts. Provenance source strings intentionally change to revision lineage, while original teacher identity and label basis remain; full provenance-object equality is therefore false, not a class-preservation failure.

findings.title: Validation is small and mechanism-held-out, not coverage-complete
findings.detail: 72 isolated groups: 60 train and 12 validation. Rule groups 1–10 train; 11–12 validation (reachability and pairwise voting). Therefore rule validation does not measure held-out examples of all trained mechanisms. Forty-eight selected rows agree with published targets, but only two per mechanism; shortest/longest heuristic selected two rejects in score group and two empty results in symmetric-difference group. Boundary examples include zero hours, exact capacity, wraparound, overlap endpoints, zero remainder and pairwise ties; no comprehensive boundary coverage claim.

findings.title: Assembler hardcodes teacher identity and zero accounting
findings.detail: Read-only source inspection: assemble.py sets teacher_alias=openai/gpt-sol and additional/pending spend to zero instead of deriving/checking producer metadata. This can materially misattribute later producers and hide later paid generation. Current manifest metadata/provenance identify those aliases and zero spend, so no demonstrated current dataset mismatch. Recommend deriving/validating those fields before using assembler with other producers. No tests or runtime assembly executed.

findings.title: Assembler storage guard is incomplete for assignment subpaths
findings.detail: assemble.py protects artifact_prefix through shard_path(), but directly joins assignment artifact_directory and published_directory afterward. Absolute or traversal subpaths can bypass prefix containment and evaluation/final guards before producer files are opened. Current published files are inside the allowed pilot directory and were independently checked; no exploit or forbidden read attempted. Enforce the same containment/excluded-storage guard on every resolved source/published path before accepting less-trusted configs. validate.py itself checks manifest shard paths before reads; no material bug found for the current valid dataset.

findings.title: Label-hidden teacher review is not independent correctness evidence
findings.detail: Label-free selected_inputs.jsonl was written first and 48 rationales frozen in precomparison_decisions.json before target comparison. Sentiment g01:r01 class P had already appeared in the revision-map excerpt, so row 13 is ordinary teacher review, not blind. Other 47 selected target labels had not been displayed when assessed; audit semantics were already read. Same exposed model alias as original teacher, different session; immutable revisions unknown. All 120 rule targets reproduced using the published expected() helper (the script has no expected_result symbol), not an independently authored solver or independently parsed text. Text spot-check helps fidelity assessment but proves neither generator nor facts correct.
